analysis:
The supplied units are BASE-side text of SSDPrefixCacheTests.swift (lines 610-1755). The only visible head change is a test-only addition near head line 3140: new tests for SSDWholeRootMaintainer header-verdict caching (ctime-aware invalidation when a header is corrupted with its mtime restored) and replaced-lookalike re-reading. The patch excerpt is truncated, and the production source (SSDWholeRootMaintainer, SSDBlockStore) is not supplied, so any production change accompanying these tests is not reviewed here.

The examined base tests cover the production gate (DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill switch), the 30-minute TTL cap, the disk-budget resolver, the isolated test-root gate requiring the ephemeral-key flag, salt isolation, HMAC-tag filenames, corrupt-block delete-and-recompute, symlink-safe removal and reconciliation, epoch stability across eviction/TTL/corruption, the endurance write cap and the overflow-safe stage floor. These exercise the T-041 mitigations (a)-(e) and the existing TTL/LRU/purge behavior. They are unchanged and weaken no controls.

The new tests reinforce the fail-closed ownership check for whole-root maintenance: a file whose header changed after an earlier pass must lose its cached ownership proof and must not be counted or deleted. No new attack surface or threat-model invalidation is visible in test-only code.

Open question for integration: if the production maintainer change adds a verdict cache keyed on file identity, size, mtime and ctime, confirm the key includes ctime and inode, and that a symlink or lookalike cannot inherit a cached owned verdict. That change is outside the supplied evidence. The tests suggest the intent is correct, but this is unverified.
